title: I released my first mobile game as a solo dev - here's where generative AI helped and where it didn't
author: DadaQuiTrade
selftext:
I recently finished and released my first mobile game, Orbit Defender.



I'm a solo developer, so one of the biggest limitations during development was obviously the amount of work one person can realistically produce.



I used generative AI for some of the visual asset work, while the actual game systems, balancing, Unity integration, UI, backend, leaderboards, Daily Challenge system and all the iteration around the gameplay still had to be built and polished normally.



One thing I found interesting is that generating an asset is often the easy part. Making everything visually consistent, readable on a phone, correctly cropped, animated, positioned and actually usable inside the game still took a lot of iteration.



The finished game is a free arcade/high-score game where you defend a planet, collect upgrades and compete through Daily Challenges and leaderboards.



Android:

[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fallentgames.orbitdefender](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fallentgames.orbitdefender)



I'd be interested to hear how other solo developers are handling the same balance between AI-assisted asset creation and keeping a game's visual identity coherent.

"I'm a solo developer, so one of the biggest limitations during development was obviously the amount of work one person can realistically produce." 

Except all the solo devs that have done and still do eactly that without the use of Gen AI.

Concerned Ape, Redigit, Localthunk, Zack (dude that made siralim games) and several others.

This idea that one person can't find the time to develop something without AI pollutes the well for all of us.

Learn to be genuine.

AI isn't the problem, people misusing and misrepresenting actual work are.

You think OP misused AI by creating assets and telling us that they used it that way? You think they "misrepresent actual work" by calling scope and time a limitation? Maybe you should start to be the least bit genuine yourself.

comments.author: Upper_Hospital_8053
comments.body:
How long did it take you from idea to publish? 
How much code experience did you have before starting it?
How are you monetizing? I noticed its free to install

Congrats on the release

replies.author: DadaQuiTrade
replies.body:
It's been 2 to 3 weeks since i'm on it, i'm not a regular dev, i started on my own with some cubes with the basics, the game had no update / survivor and Roguelite Mechanic's, I was using AI as a mentor to help me learn unity's environment. 

Then after i asked it to correct some scripts when i was totally lost, it helped me debug also :)

The game is 100% free (you still can buy some coins for cosmetics but that's all) all the monetization is made with rewarded ads, only consented by user (for revive / x2 coins or changing an upgrade)
